Optimal Binning for Numerical Variables using Order-Restricted Bayesian Evidence

Source: R/obn_orbe.R
ob_numerical_orbe.Rd

Chooses the cutpoints and the number of bins that maximize a Bayesian score of a piecewise-constant event rate, with the shape of the Weight of Evidence (monotone, peak or valley) enforced inside an exact dynamic program. Reports posterior-mean WoE with credible intervals.

Usage

ob_numerical_orbe(
  feature,
  target,
  min_bins = 2,
  max_bins = 10,
  bin_cutoff = 0.05,
  max_n_prebins = 200,
  monotonic_trend = "auto",
  prior_strength = 1,
  credible_level = 0.95,
  bin_penalty = 0,
  criterion = "predictive"
)

Arguments

feature

A numeric vector of feature values. NA and NaN rows are excluded from the fit. -Inf and +Inf are kept and fall in the first and last bin.

target

A binary vector (0/1 or logical) with the same length as feature. Missing values are an error.

min_bins

Minimum number of bins (default: 2). It is honored whenever a partition with that many bins satisfies the shape and bin_cutoff; otherwise the largest feasible number of bins is returned. With min_bins = 1 a single bin is returned when the score does not support any cut.

max_bins

Maximum number of bins (default: 10). The number of bins is selected by the score between min_bins and max_bins, so max_bins is an upper limit, not a target.

bin_cutoff

Minimum fraction of the non-missing rows in a bin, in \([0, 1)\) (default: 0.05). It is a constraint of the optimization.

max_n_prebins

Maximum number of atoms, the candidate units the bins are built from (default: 200). A feature with at most this many distinct values is searched over every boundary between distinct values. Above it, adjacent distinct values are grouped into atoms of about equal frequency, which restricts the candidate cutpoints. Values above 1000 are treated as 1000, and the limit is lowered further when max_bins is large, to bound memory.

monotonic_trend

Shape of the WoE across bins: "auto" (default; ascending or descending, whichever has the larger score), "ascending", "descending", "peak" (increasing then decreasing), "valley" (decreasing then increasing) or "none".

prior_strength

Weight of the prior, in pseudo-events of the minority class (default: 1). Larger values shrink the WoE of small bins more strongly toward zero.

credible_level

Probability content of the WoE credible intervals, in \((0, 1)\) (default: 0.95).

bin_penalty

Cost of each bin beyond the first, in units of the log score, at most 1e6 (default: 0). Positive values give fewer bins and guard against splitting a feature unrelated to the target.

criterion

Score of a bin: "predictive" (default), the leave-one-out log predictive probability of its rows, or "evidence", its log marginal likelihood. "predictive" favors out-of-sample accuracy and returns more bins; "evidence" is more parsimonious and, with a positive bin_penalty, recovers the number of distinct event-rate levels more often. See Details.

Value

A list with one element per bin in the vectors below:

id

Bin identifiers (1-based).

bin

Interval labels, e.g. "(-Inf;1.500000]".

woe

Posterior-mean Weight of Evidence.

iv

Information Value contribution, \((p_i - q_i) \, \mathrm{WoE}_i\), with \(p_i\) and \(q_i\) the observed shares of events and non-events.

count, count_pos, count_neg

Rows, events and non-events.

event_rate

Observed event rate.

woe_se

Posterior standard deviation of the WoE.

woe_lower, woe_upper

Limits of the equal-tailed credible interval of the WoE.

and the following:

cutpoints

Upper limits of all bins but the last.

total_iv

Sum of iv.

total_iv_corrected

total_iv minus the first-order sampling bias of a plug-in IV, floored at zero.

log_score

Score of the selected partition.

log_score_by_bins

Score of the best partition with \(1, 2, \ldots\) bins under the selected shape; NA where no partition is feasible.

criterion

The criterion used.

monotonic_trend

Shape of the selected model.

order_probability

Posterior probability that the bin event rates follow the selected shape.

converged

Always TRUE: the search is exact.

iterations

Number of bin counts evaluated.

Details

Model. Let bin \(i\) hold \(n_i\) rows and \(e_i\) events, and let \(\pi_0\) be the overall event rate. The event rates of the bins are independent \(\mathrm{Beta}(a, b)\) with mean \(\pi_0\) and \(\min(a, b)\) equal to prior_strength, which is the uniform prior when \(\pi_0 = 0.5\). Write \(A_i = a + e_i\) and \(B_i = b + n_i - e_i\).

Criterion. A partition is scored by \(\sum_i f(n_i, e_i)\) minus bin_penalty for each bin beyond the first. With criterion = "predictive", \(f\) is the leave-one-out log predictive probability of the rows of the bin, each row predicted from the posterior given the other rows of its bin: $$f(n_i, e_i) = e_i \log\frac{A_i - 1}{A_i + B_i - 1} + (n_i - e_i) \log\frac{B_i - 1}{A_i + B_i - 1} .$$ With criterion = "evidence", \(f\) is the log marginal likelihood $$f(n_i, e_i) = \log \frac{B(A_i, B_i)}{B(a, b)} .$$ Both scores fall when a bin is split into bins with equal observed event rates: by about one unit for the predictive score, and by an amount that grows as \(\frac{1}{2}\log n_i\) for the evidence, which therefore returns fewer bins in large samples. The cutpoints are chosen among many candidates, so with bin_penalty = 0 a feature unrelated to the target can still be split, more often under "predictive". A positive bin_penalty controls this: it multiplies the prior weight of a partition by \(e^{-\mathrm{penalty}}\) for each additional bin.

Optimization. The engine maximizes the score over all partitions into contiguous bins that respect bin_cutoff, the limits on the number of bins and the shape. The state of the dynamic program is the last bin of a partial partition, and a bin may follow another only when its posterior WoE respects the shape, so the reported WoE satisfies the shape strictly. The search is exact over the atoms and takes \(O(K u^2 \log u)\) time for \(u\) atoms.

Order restriction. Restricting \(K\) exchangeable rates to an order multiplies the marginal likelihood by the ratio of the posterior to the prior probability of that order. The prior probability is \(1/K!\) for a given monotone direction, \(2/K!\) for "auto" and \(2^{K-1}/K!\) for a peak or a valley. The logarithm of this ratio is added to the score of the best partition of each size before the number of bins and, for "auto", the direction are selected. order_probability is the posterior probability in that ratio.

WoE. The reported WoE is the posterior mean $$\mathrm{WoE}_i = \psi(A_i) - \psi(B_i) - \log\frac{\pi_0}{1 - \pi_0},$$ where \(\psi\) is the digamma function. Its posterior variance is \(\psi'(A_i) + \psi'(B_i)\) and the interval limits are the logits of the Beta quantiles. The WoE is finite for bins without events or without non-events. The credible intervals are conditional on the selected bins.

References

Boullé, M. (2006). MODL: A Bayes optimal discretization method for continuous attributes. Machine Learning, 65(1), 131-165.

Geisser, S., & Eddy, W. F. (1979). A predictive approach to model selection. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 74(365), 153-160.

Barlow, R. E., Bartholomew, D. J., Bremner, J. M., & Brunk, H. D. (1972). Statistical inference under order restrictions. John Wiley & Sons.

See also

ob_categorical_orbe for categorical features, ob_numerical_ir for isotonic regression binning and ob_numerical_mdlp for entropy-based binning.

Examples

set.seed(123)
feature <- rnorm(2000)
target <- rbinom(2000, 1, plogis(-2 + 0.8 * feature))

fit <- ob_numerical_orbe(feature, target)

# Bins, posterior-mean WoE and its credible interval
data.frame(
  bin = fit$bin, count = fit$count,
  woe = round(fit$woe, 3),
  lower = round(fit$woe_lower, 3),
  upper = round(fit$woe_upper, 3)
)
#>                     bin count    woe  lower  upper
#> 1      (-Inf;-1.185480]   230 -1.703 -2.550 -0.993
#> 2 (-1.185480;-0.457761]   390 -1.100 -1.578 -0.667
#> 3 (-0.457761;-0.191775]   200 -0.649 -1.194 -0.159
#> 4 (-0.191775;-0.060822]   110 -0.169 -0.767  0.368
#> 5  (-0.060822;0.354352]   320 -0.037 -0.369  0.275
#> 6   (0.354352;0.818828]   310  0.314  0.017  0.597
#> 7   (0.818828;1.181181]   200  0.451  0.099  0.786
#> 8   (1.181181;1.532424]   110  0.781  0.353  1.188
#> 9       (1.532424;+Inf]   130  1.330  0.979  1.674

# Score of the best partition for each number of bins
round(fit$log_score_by_bins, 1)
#>  [1] -790.7 -742.3 -726.4 -722.6 -720.0 -717.7 -716.1 -715.3 -714.7 -714.7
fit$monotonic_trend
#> [1] "ascending"

# A more parsimonious fit
fit_ev <- ob_numerical_orbe(feature, target, criterion = "evidence")
length(fit_ev$bin)
#> [1] 8

# A non-monotone relationship
target2 <- rbinom(2000, 1, plogis(-1 - feature^2))
fit2 <- ob_numerical_orbe(feature, target2, monotonic_trend = "peak")
round(fit2$woe, 3)
#>  [1] -3.582 -0.908  0.064  0.456  0.889  0.365  0.127 -0.643 -1.159 -3.582
